spot.html_text: The list of various equivalent axiomatizations of CT ⟦S⟧ can be further extended with two more innocent-looking principles. The first one considers the truth conditions for disjunctions with arbitrary finite number of disjuncts. More precisely, the principle, called disjunctive correctness (DC), expresses that for every n and for every collection of formulas ⟦M⟧ the disjunction ⟦M⟧ is true if and only if there is ⟦M⟧ such that ⟦M⟧ is true. spot.html_text: Theories of truth and predication are closely related to theories of properties and property attribution. To say that an open formula ⟦M⟧ is true of an individual ⟦M⟧ seems equivalent (in some sense) to the claim that ⟦M⟧ has the property of being such that ⟦M⟧ (this property is signified by the open formula).
